claims.text: An as-deposited high-entropy-alloy coating can have a predominantly single-phase BCC microstructure before secondary-phase development.
Deliberately incorporating nanoscale multilayer interfaces promotes a refined and more uniform distribution of secondary phases or precipitate-like features.
Secondary HCP-like phases can emerge from an initially BCC high-entropy alloy.
Secondary phases or precipitate-like features at multilayer interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Interface-induced dislocation pinning is responsible for improved creep resistance in high-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings.
Coherent nanoscale interfaces impede dislocation glide by acting as stress barriers.
Coherent nanoscale interfaces impede grain-boundary sliding.
A refined distribution of secondary phase at interfaces enhances creep resistance through a precipitation-hardening-like effect.
The combined interface and secondary-phase effects reduce dislocation mobility and delay plastic deformation under prolonged stress.
At identical high-temperature and stress conditions, multilayer coatings will have lower creep strain rates than monolithic coatings of the same overall composition and thickness.
At identical high-temperature and stress conditions, multilayer coatings will have longer times to failure than corresponding monolithic coatings.
At identical high-temperature and stress conditions, multilayer coatings will show a delayed onset of measurable plastic deformation.
The interfacial benefit may be reduced when individual layers exceed an optimal nanoscale thickness.
Processing imperfections that reduce interface coherence may limit the creep-resistance benefit.
Residual stresses introduced during deposition may modify the creep response.
Creep testing near 982 °C under constant load is an applicable comparison condition.
The comparison should use a monolithic control with the same overall composition and thickness as the multilayer coating.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant decrease in creep rate or increase in time to failure in the multilayer coating would falsify the proposed interfacial mechanism.
